feed.title: Bounds on chain length with BIP-54 timewarp fixes

entry.title: Bounds on chain length with BIP-54 timewarp fixes
entry.summary:
The proposal to replace the existing two BIP-54 timewarp rules with a monotonic timestamp requirement seeks to simplify the proof process for blockchain difficulty adjustments by eliminating the allowance of negative solvetimes, which currently enables the Difficulty Adjustment Algorithm (DAA) to perceive "negative work" and subsequently lower the difficulty. This change could ensure that timestamps always move forward, thereby potentially stabilizing the mining process by disallowing periods where time effectively moves backward.
The mathematical implications of implementing a monotonic timestamp rule are significant yet subtle. The proposed formula for calculating the upper bound on block length under this new rule would be $$ u(t,w) \approx \frac{t}{600} + 1397.385\log_2 w - 57830.9 $$ blocks. This represents a minor adjustment from the current BIP-54 formula, which is $$ u(t,w) \approx \frac{t}{596.4285} + 1405.753\log_2 w - 58189.3 $$. The difference in maximum chain lengths between these two formulas is approximately 0.6%, equating to around 7200 seconds over a two-week period. This comparative analysis highlights that while the impact of such a change might seem minor numerically, it could have meaningful effects on the blockchain's operational stability and security.
